messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Canary alert — high 5xx rate on deployment model-runtime-canary-2 in prod (traffic 3%). Observed spike starting 1719994300. Error: upstream 502s from model-container.

DeployBot: Deploy 2024.11.02-9843 started canary -> pods(model-runtime-canary-2-*) running image registry.internal.redwood/model-runtime:stable-20241102

Alex K: oncall here, looking. Any customer-facing errors?

Priya R: I see increased 502s in frontend logs routed to /v1/generate. Affected requests mostly from eu-west-1. Canary traffic is low but errors correlate with new image.

Dan: copying logs, sample 502s: 
```
2024-11-02T18:45:12Z ERROR runtime: handler failed: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to load model weights: checksum mismatch
```

Mei: checksum mismatch => possible corrupted artifact in image layer or wrong image pushed. I'll pull the canary image locally to inspect.

Priya R: Can't repro locally yet, but registry tags look odd. Someone retagged `stable-20241102` to point at a previously unpublished build id.

Alex K: Do we have a kill switch on the feature flag for canary routing? SRE Runbook: where's the route config?

SRE Runbook: Canary routing is via traffic-router service configured in Consul. Feature flag key: rollout/model-runtime/canary. Toggle is available in Console -> Feature Flags. Runbook step to kill canary: `flagctl set rollout/model-runtime/canary false` then confirm router picks it up.

Priya R: I'm toggling flag now -> `flagctl set rollout/model-runtime/canary false`

Priya R: :white_check_mark: flag set to false. Traffic should shift back to stable pool in ~10s. Monitoring: error rate dropping in the canary subset but still seeing 502s from the initial batch.

Alex K: Great. Next: we need to revert the bad image in registry and roll the canary back to the known-good digest. Dan, can you fetch the previous digest?

Dan: grabbing publish logs from CI: last good image digest for stable before 2024.11.02 was sha256:fa34b7c2d9e6. Latest publish (9843) pushed sha256:badd1ff00d... which doesn't match content checks. Suspect cache poisoning in our CI artifact mirror.

Mei: local pull output: `docker image inspect registry.internal.redwood/model-runtime@sha256:badd1ff00d` returns unexpected layers and checksum mismatch.

Priya R: We should delete the bad tag to prevent future pulls: `gcrctl delete-tag registry/internal/model-runtime:stable-20241102` but need approvals for destructive ops. Suggest we 1) undeploy canary traffic (done), 2) rollback deployments to previous replicaset/digest, 3) mark the CI publish as failed and revoke tag.

Alex K: Agreed. Dan, do the rollback. Priya, start a mitigation CR to block the tag in artifact mirrors. Mei, collect the failing request ids for customer impact.

Dan: Rolling back canary now: `kubectl -n prod rollout undo deployment/model-runtime --to-revision=12` -> running.

DeployBot: Rollout status: rollback started. Old replicaset stable-12 scaling up, new-canary scaling down.

Dan: Post-rollback health checks: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" https://model-api.prod/health` -> 200. Metrics show 5xx back to baseline within 45s.

Priya R: Filing mitigation ticket: MIT-2024-780 created. Blocking tag propagation on mirror: mirror-block set for stable-20241102 across eu mirrors.

Alex K: Customer impact? Mei?

Mei: Looking at error sampling: ~0.8% of total requests for the hour hit canary and failed. A handful of enterprise customers routed to canary via VIP experienced transient 502s (~15 sessions). No data exfiltration, errors are load-time model init failures.

Alex K: Ok, we should page CS for customer outreach to those tenants. Priya, can you list customer IDs?

Priya R: Customer IDs: CUST-1982, CUST-4482, CUST-7011. I'll loop in support@ and drop a brief note.

Dan: I also found CI job logs showing an intermittent registry race: publish job sometimes reuses a mutable tag then quickly reassigns digests — root cause likely our mirror promotion script that retags latest -> stable after manifest replication completes. If replication lagged, a previous manifest got tagged.

Alex K: Action items: 1) rollback performed and confirmed, 2) tag blocked and mirror paused (Priya), 3) CI job flagged (Dan) and we should add strict digest-based publish (no mutable tag until replicated), 4) postmortem assigned.

Priya R: Adding SRE and Release Eng to incident: @Dan @Mei @Alex K @ReleaseEng. Starting post-incident triage doc now.

Mei: Collecting extra logs and saving failing images to quarantine registry: `gcrctl mirror --quarantine registry/internal/model-runtime@sha256:badd1ff00d`

Dan: I'm assigning root-cause analysis to myself and ReleaseEng team. We'll reproduce mirror promotion script locally.

SRE Runbook: Handoff: Next on-call is Priya R at 1720002400. Please continue mitigation steps and update MIT ticket.

Alex K: Handing off to Priya. Leaving note: rollback successful, tags blocked, customers notified, RCA assigned to Dan + ReleaseEng. Postmortem owner: Dan.

Priya R: Acknowledged. Will monitor for 2h, escalate if any regression. Opening CS thread and adding merchant impact notes.

DeployBot: :white_check_mark: Canary removed from traffic. Current distribution: stable pool 100%.

IncidentBot: Incident MIT-2024-780 created and linked. Severity: P2 (partial customer impact). Pager notifications sent to oncall and release-eng.

Alex K: Thanks team. Postmortem checklist: include timeline, CI publish logs, registry replication latency graphs, and patch to mirror promotion script.

Priya R: Will add playbook step to prevent mutable-tag promotion until manifest digest confirmed on all mirrors.

Dan: I'll pull a patch request and add integration test to CI to ensure tag immutability on promotion.

Mei: Adding saved artifacts and sanitized logs to the MIT ticket for follow-up.

Alex K: Closing handoff. If anything else pops, page me. :thumbsup:

Priya R: :thumbsup: 1719998840 — taking over monitoring.
